description: EMBOSS 6.6.0 showfeat: the features of the sequences of a file (any input format of seqret that carries features) as lines of ASCII graphics under a scale: one line per feature (or per part of a join; with joinFeatures the parts of a join on one line, with collapse the features on the same line) with the strand (|---> for forward, <---| for reverse), optionally the strand, source, positions, type and tags with their values. The features are filtered by sourceMatch, typeMatch, tagMatch and valueMatch (wildcards * and ?, several patterns separated by blanks, commas, semicolons or bars; stricttags shows only the tags that match), sorted (sort: start, source, type or nosort; by strand first), the sense is selected by forward / reverse / unknown, and annotation adds ranges with a text ("5-10 foo,20-30 bar") as lines of their own. width is the width of the graphics (below 4 no graphics and no scale), html wraps the output in HTML. Equals the installed program on 1 000 runs (every input format with features, every option, damaged files, the runs on which the program dies by a fault). A5-8c3h, B09 F260.

sequence.description: The text of the sequence file with features (see the formats above), or a sequence as letters (no features).

sequenceFormat.description: The input format (-sformat); default: the program finds the format.

sourceMatch.description: Sources of the features to show (-sourcematch); default *.

typeMatch.description: Types of the features to show (-typematch); default *.

tagMatch.description: Tags a feature must have (-tagmatch); default *.

valueMatch.description: Values the tag must have (-valuematch); default *.

sort.description: Sort order (-sort): start (default), source, type or nosort.

joinFeatures.description: Show the parts of a join on one line (-joinfeatures).

id.description: Show the name of the sequence (-id); default true.

description.description: Show the description of the sequence (-description); default true.

scale.description: Show the scale line (-scale); default true.

width.description: Width of the graphics lines (-width); default 60; below 4 there are no graphics and no scale; negative values are reset to 0 with a warning.

collapse.description: Show all features of a type on one line (-collapse).

unknown.description: Show features of unknown sense (-unknown); default true.

showStrand.description: Show the strand of the features (-strand).

showValues.description: Show the values of the tags (-valueshow); default true.

strictTags.description: Show only the tags that match tagMatch and valueMatch (-stricttags).

annotation.description: Ranges to show as annotation (-annotation): "5-10 text,20-30 text".

qualifiers.description: Sequence input qualifiers as typed after the sequence on the command line: -sbegin1 -send1 -sreverse1, -slower1 -supper1 -snucleotide1 -sprotein1 -scircular1, -sformat1 F, -sid1 name, -sdbname1 db, -squick1, -iquery1 query, -ioffset1 bytes.

files.description: More files by name (file name -> text) that sequenceValue may name.

sequenceValue.description: The USA of the sequence input (-sequence): [format::]file[begin:end:r], file:id, file:field:value, file{a|b}, @list, list::list, asis::TEXT, db:id; the text of sequence is the file 'sequence.dat'.

definitions.description: The text of an EMBOSS configuration file (.embossrc) that defines databases for sequenceValue: DBNAME definitions (methods direct, emboss and emblcd), RES / RESOURCE, SERVER, INCLUDE (the included file is an entry of files), IF / IFDEF / ELSE / ENDIF and SET blocks; the files of a database, and for the methods emboss (dbxfasta / dbxflat index files NAME.ent, .xid, .pxid ...) and emblcd (dbifasta / dbiflat files division.lkp, entrynam.idx, acnum.trg ...) its index files as latin-1 text, are entries of files by path.

text.description: The text of the output file.

messages.description: What the library printed (warnings and errors).

errors.message: Unable to read sequence ... (no sequence in the file)
Bad range value ... / Odd integer(s) in range specification (annotation)
An input on which the reference program never stops or dies by a fault is refused
